notes: Hand-verified against the scenario's own arithmetic before comparing to reference-model output. This scenario reuses DEBT-001's exact loan ($60,000.00, 6% annual, 60-month equal-principal amortization), so month m's interest is identical to DEBT-001's: interest_m = 300.00 − 5.00×(m−1) (see DEBT-001's approval.json for the full derivation). Monthly revenue (3000.00) less expense (1000.00) nets to the same 2000.00/month DEBT-001 used directly, so every income-statement and cash figure below reduces to DEBT-001's own formulas with the partnership's $20,000.00 combined opening contribution (vs. DEBT-001's $70,000.00 single-owner contribution) in place of DEBT-001's opening balance.

Monthly net income_m = 2000.00 − interest_m = 1700.00 + 5.00×(m−1). Monthly net cash flow_m = 2000.00 − payment_m (payment_m = interest_m + 1000.00 principal) = 700.00 + 5.00×(m−1) — the identical per-month cash-change formula as DEBT-001 (since the $1000.00/month revenue-less-expense delta here matches DEBT-001's $2000.00 flat revenue only after also netting the $1000.00 principal, both scenarios ultimately reducing to the same loan cash flows on top of otherwise-identical $2000.00/month net operating cash).
Cumulative cash through month M: 80000.00 (20000.00 contributions + 60000.00 loan proceeds, both day 1) + 700.00×M + 2.5×M×(M−1).
